script.title: Why the Leaning Tower of Pisa Is Also Curved
sentences: The tower was only two floors high when it started sinking.
This was Pisa in 1178, and its three-metre foundation sat in weak, unstable soil.
Then construction stopped for the better part of a century.
When work resumed, engineers built the upper floors taller on one side to make up for the tilt.
So the tower is actually curved.
The job took 199 years in all.
That long pause happened because Pisa was almost always at war with Genoa, Lucca and Florence, and it let the soil settle.
Without it, the tower would almost certainly have toppled.
script.description:
The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to sink in 1178.
A century-long pause is the reason it is still standing.
visuals: Leaning Tower of Pisa close up arcades
claims_en: In 1178 the tower began to sink after construction progressed to the second floor.
The tower had a three-metre foundation set in weak, unstable subsoil.
Construction was halted for the better part of a century.
To compensate for the tilt, engineers built upper floors with one side taller than the other.
Because of this, the tower is curved.
Construction occurred in three stages over 199 years.
Construction was halted because the Republic of Pisa was almost continually engaged in battles with Genoa, Lucca and Florence.
The halt allowed time for the underlying soil to settle.
Otherwise, the tower would almost certainly have toppled.
